title: UniCAIM: A Unified CAM/CIM Architecture with Static-Dynamic KV Cache Pruning for Efficient Long-Context LLM Inference
problem: Transformer LLM inference on long sequences suffers from massive KV cache memory and computation overhead; existing CIM accelerators support only static pruning with fixed patterns or inefficient dynamic pruning.
motivation: Long-context LLM inference is memory-bound due to KV cache quadratic growth; pruning can reduce overhead but requires flexible hardware support.
method: The processor (UniCAIM) uses FeFET transistors—hardware cells storing multiple values each—with three operating modes: constant-time filtering of key-value pairs through approximate similarity search, applying preset filtering patterns, or performing exact attention calculations through electrical-current operations. Because storage and computation occur directly in the transistor cells, it avoids expensive data transfers between components.
key_novelty: First chip design that combines content-searching and in-memory computing to filter AI model caches using both preset patterns and real-time analysis, with transistors storing multiple values for efficient computation without data movement.
contributions: Three computation modes for flexible pruning strategies
Novel CAM/CIM cell design for signed multibit storage
8.2x to 831x AEDP reduction vs SOTA CIM accelerators at circuit level
High accuracy comparable with dense attention at application level

metrics.other: 8.2x to 831x AEDP reduction vs SOTA CIM, comparable accuracy to dense attention

primary_theme: unified CAM/CIM for flexible KV cache pruning in LLM inference
